name: Dieppe
title: Dieppe Ship Thickness Gauging | UTM for Ferries & Cargo
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Dieppe, Normandy: Newhaven ferry, reefer and timber ships, scallop trawlers and coasters, with hull, tank and piping UTM.
h1: Ultrasonic Hull Gauging in Dieppe, Normandy
intro: Dieppe is a Normandy port with a ferry link to Newhaven, a fruit terminal, timber and aggregates traffic and one of the Channel's well-known scallop fleets. Ships here are modest in size but regular in their calls, which suits planned gauging between sailings. A team travels from India to Dieppe and works at the ferry berth, the cargo quays and the fishing basin, with the plan set by tide and timetable.

highlights.p: A ro-pax ferry on the Newhaven crossing runs inside the SECA, which wears piping and decks quickly. Layover time at Dieppe is limited, so gauging is planned around the timetable and extended during any refit period.

Reefers, timber carriers and aggregate ships use the commercial quays, often for a day or two. They are good candidates for deck, hatch and tank gauging between cargo operations, planned with the agent and the stevedores.
Dieppe's fishing boats work a scallop season and return to the fishing basin for gear and repairs. Hull, tank and deck gauging fits the weeks when boats are in harbour and the fishery is closed.

port.h: Dieppe: a Channel harbour with a ferry berth, cargo quays and a working fishing basin
p: Dieppe sits in a gap in the Normandy cliffs on the Channel coast, with a tidal approach channel between two piers leading to the port's basins. The harbour is managed on behalf of the Normandy region, and the commercial quays, the ferry terminal and the fishing basin lie close together around the town centre. Tidal range on this coast is large, and the depth available in the channel and the inner basins varies with the state of the tide, so ship movements are scheduled around high water and pilots are used regularly.

The passenger link is the ferry to Newhaven on the English south coast, a route that has run through Dieppe for generations and still carries cars, passengers and freight. On the cargo side, Dieppe handles imported fruit in refrigerated ships, timber, sand and aggregates, and general cargo carried by small coasters. The fishing basin supports a fleet of trawlers and smaller boats, notably those working scallops in the Channel, with a fish market and processing businesses nearby. Tugs, pilot boats and dredging craft working the approach add to the local fleet.

Dieppe's seasons and tides shape the inspection calendar. The scallop season runs through the colder months, so fishing boats are most available for gauging in the closed season. Reefer calls follow the fruit import cycle and are regular and short. Ferries run all year, with a winter maintenance period when the ship may go to a yard elsewhere. Westerly gales and a heavy swell at the harbour entrance can hold up arrivals and departures, which sometimes gives a ship a longer stay than its schedule had planned, and a flexible team can use it.

facilities.h: Where ships can be gauged at Dieppe
p: The ferry berth is a working terminal with ramps and passenger buildings, so gauging there concentrates on what the crew can release during the layover. Vehicle deck plating, ramp structure, machinery piping and the scrubber lines of ferries that have them are the usual targets, with tanks added when the schedule allows. Larger scope, such as full ballast tank and shell programmes, is usually done in a refit period, and the readings taken at Dieppe help the yard define the steel scope.

The commercial quays take reefers, timber ships and aggregate carriers for a day or two at a time, and a team can gauge hatch covers, coamings, deck plating and the accessible tanks during cargo gaps. In the fishing basin, trawlers lie alongside between trips, and the owner or skipper can release tanks, fish holds and deck areas for gauging when the boat is cleaned. Dieppe's repair capacity suits smaller boats and workboats, and ships needing a full docking generally go to a larger yard in another port.
list: Ferry berth — vehicle deck, ramp and machinery piping gauging between sailings and during layovers.
Commercial quays — hatch cover, coaming, deck and tank gauging on reefers, timber ships and aggregate carriers.
Fishing basin — hull, tank and deck gauging on scallop trawlers and smaller boats between trips.
Inner basin lay-by berths — longer condition gauging on coasters and workboats laid by between jobs.
Outer harbour and roads — anchorage work on waiting ships when the sea allows a launch.

context.h: French port state control, the SECA and the cross-Channel link at Dieppe
p: In France, the Centres de sécurité des navires of the Affaires maritimes administration carry out port state control under the Paris MoU, and ships calling at Dieppe may be inspected like any others in the Channel. Ro-pax ferries are subject to the EU survey regime for ferries on regular service, and their class society sets the extent of structural gauging. Fishing vessels follow French fishing vessel safety rules and many are unclassed, so a thickness report often serves an owner, a buyer or an insurer.

Dieppe lies in the part of the Channel covered by the North Sea SECA, so scrubber-fitted ships run their wash-water systems on every sailing and overboard piping is a high-wear item. The EU emissions trading scheme and FuelEU Maritime apply to the larger ships, and the Inventory of Hazardous Materials is required for those above the size threshold. For owners of older coasters and reefers, a clear measured record of steel condition makes it easier to decide whether to refit, sell or retire the ship.

jobs.p: Jobs at Dieppe are usually short and planned. We agree the scope with the superintendent or the skipper, check the tide and the cargo programme, and bring a small team sized to the work. Results are delivered by space or by deck, in the class format where the ship is classed, and in a simpler owner's format for unclassed fishing boats. Where the ship will dock elsewhere, the report is arranged so the yard can use it for its steel estimate.
list: Vehicle deck, ramp and piping gauging on a ferry during a layover, ahead of a winter refit at another yard.
Hatch cover and coaming gauging on a timber or reefer ship alongside during a cargo gap.
Hull and tank gauging on a scallop trawler in the closed season, for the owner or an insurer.
Scrubber wash-water piping gauging on a ro-pax ferry or coaster that trades inside the SECA.
Pre-purchase condition gauging on an older coaster laid by in the inner basin.

logistics: Paris Charles de Gaulle is the usual arrival point, with onward travel by rail or road through Rouen to Dieppe; Rouen and Beauvais regional airports are alternatives. Technicians travel from India on Schengen visas applied for when dates are firm, with an invitation letter from the owner or manager. Access to the ferry terminal, the quays and the fishing basin is arranged through the ship's agent or the owner, and plans allow for tide and weather at the harbour entrance.

faqs.q: Can you gauge the Newhaven ferry at Dieppe?
faqs.a: Yes, within the layover the operator allows. Vehicle deck plating, ramps and hinge areas, machinery piping and scrubber lines can be measured while the ship is alongside, and tanks are added when released. Anything larger is best planned for a refit period, and the Dieppe readings help define the steel scope for that yard stay.

faqs.q: How does the tide affect gauging at Dieppe?
faqs.a: Ships enter and leave the basins at suitable states of tide, so time alongside can be short or long depending on the cargo and the tide table. We plan the scope around the expected stay, begin with the priority spaces, and extend the programme only if the ship's stay allows it.

faqs.q: Can scallop trawlers be gauged in Dieppe?
faqs.a: Yes, ideally during the closed season or a repair stop. We gauge hulls, tanks, fish holds and deck structure around winches and gantries once the spaces are clean and safe to enter. The report is simple and by area, which suits owners, insurers and buyers who may not have class documentation.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock for ships that need steel renewal near Dieppe?
faqs.a: Dieppe's repair capacity is limited to smaller vessels, and larger ships usually dock at a bigger yard in another port. Gauging at Dieppe provides the measured thickness the yard needs to scope and plan its steel work, and a single Schengen visa covers a docking elsewhere in France or Belgium.
